title: consumer-twin
description: NX-042 T1 (design §2, D1, D4, D5, D7): one version of a consumer twin - the explicit hypotheses, the decision-layer parameters and the generator version. Hypotheses are statements, never facts. Every behaviour parameter is an interval (D4: no single probability). A twin holds no real content (D5): parameters and hypotheses only; it is kept for good and is not deleted with a simulation world (its events in a world are, NX-041 D2). The owner publishes a version through a governed Action (D7); the server assigns the version, freezes it, keeps the publisher's calibration report reference (informational) and keeps its status as appended events (published, retired). Its calibration is a separate appended event (report reference, verdict, time; written by NX-042 T5 after checking the report); the frozen calibration status is derived from the latest event, uncalibrated without a passed one, and NX-043 cannot select an uncalibrated version. Hypothesis statements and the description must not look like real content (an email, 7+ digits, a member-style number, a 32+ hex identifier).

additionalProperties.description: A behaviour's probability as an interval at its nominal coverage, and the hypotheses it rests on. D4: high - low >= 0.01 (low = high would be a single probability); JSON Schema cannot compare the two, so SQL (runtime.nexloop_twin_min_interval_width) and nexloop_eios.consumer_twins enforce it, and the bounds below keep both ends off the degenerate edges.

frozen.description: Server-derived at publication, never accepted from the publisher.
